name: How I Became a Pokémon Card
englishName: How I Became a Pokémon Card

description.text:
Kagemaru Himeno, one of the card game's illustrators, wrote How I Became a Pokémon Card (ポケモンカードになったワケ), a manga in six volumes in which each chapter tells the story behind one of her card illustrations. Each volume came with a card she drew for it, in a paper envelope mounted inside the book: Mankey with volume 1 on 22 May 1999, then Psyduck (September 1999), Jynx (January 2000), Sunkern (August 2000), Hoppip (July 2001) and, with the last volume on 22 September 2001, the birthday Pikachu, "_____'s Pikachu".

The cards print no number. The first five name themselves bonus cards of the Pokémon Card Books along their bottom edge and carry the series' mark, a small card on an open book, in place of a set symbol; the Pikachu has neither. Wizards of the Coast later printed the Psyduck's art in English as Black Star promo 20.

description.text:
How I Became a Pokémon Card (ポケモンカードになったワケ) is a manga series by Kagemaru Himeno, one of the card game's illustrators, in six volumes from 1999 to 2001. Each chapter tells the story behind one of her card illustrations, and each volume came with a card of her own, in a paper envelope mounted inside the book.

This card came with volume 1, published on 22 May 1999, whose seventh chapter, "Mankey, Mankey and Primeape", is about her Jungle Mankey and Primeape cards. Its bottom edge names it a bonus card of the Pokémon Card Books "How I Became a Pokémon Card", and in place of a set symbol it has the series' mark, a small card on an open book, which five of the six cards carry.

Wizards of the Coast printed the same art in English as Black Star promo 20, given out through the Pokémon League in September 2000.

How I Became a Pokémon Card (ポケモンカードになったワケ) is a manga series by Kagemaru Himeno, one of the card game's illustrators, in six volumes from 1999 to 2001. Each chapter tells the story behind one of her card illustrations, and each volume came with a card of her own, in a paper envelope mounted inside the book.

This card came with volume 6, the last, published on 22 September 2001, whose final chapter, "Akari and Pikachu's Birthday", tells its story. Its name leaves a blank for the owner's, its attack is called Birthday, and a box at the bottom has room to write a trainer's name and birthday. It is the only one of the six without the series' card-and-book mark, and its bottom edge says only that it can't be used in official tournaments.
